title: Promptly Task Batch
description: Structured GitHub issue proposals for one PRD section. Before publication, the consumer must validate requirement references, Project options, unique task IDs, and dependency resolution and cycles. A batch with open questions remains under review. Existing Project automations retain their configured workflow responsibilities.

feature.description: Target PRD section, such as PRD-03. The consumer must verify that the section exists.

tasks.description: Zero to five bounded task proposals, each independently verifiable after its dependencies complete. Return [] when no task can be proposed without unresolved planning decisions.

task_id.description: Stable task ID with an uppercase alphanumeric prefix and at least three digits, such as PLAY-002. Unique within the batch; reuse the ID for the same logical task across revisions.

work_type.description: Exact Work Type value from the existing GitHub Project configuration.

area.description: Exact Area value from the existing GitHub Project configuration. The consumer must validate it against the configured options before publication.

priority.description: Exact Priority value from the existing GitHub Project configuration.

requirements.description: PRD requirement references this task implements, investigates, fixes, or documents. Use numbered IDs such as F03.4 or F08.2. Use precise section headings or anchors when IDs are absent. The consumer must verify that each reference resolves in Docs/PRD.md. Cite related architecture sections or decision records in notes.

objective.description: One bounded outcome, independently reviewable and verifiable after the declared dependencies complete.

scope.description: Work explicitly included. Identify affected components, reuse boundaries, and integration points when known; distinguish existing components from planned work.

acceptance_criteria.description: Observable pass/fail conditions with concrete inputs and expected outcomes, relevant boundary or failure cases, and specific behavior to preserve. Use plain statements; the issue renderer adds checkboxes.

verification.description: Task-specific tests, build checks, or manual scenarios and the evidence required for acceptance. Include applicable repository checks and identify validation that needs particular hardware or a person.

dependencies.description: Blocking task IDs within this batch or canonical https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/NUMBER URLs for existing issues. Use [] for none. The consumer must reject duplicate, unknown, self, or cyclic dependencies, resolve task IDs to issues, and configure the matching native GitHub blocking relationships.

out_of_scope.description: Adjacent work explicitly excluded to keep the task bounded. Use [] only when there are no meaningful exclusions.

notes.description: Additional technical constraints, source paths, decision or research references, and known risks. Use an empty string when there is no additional context.

open_questions.description: Unresolved planning decisions that hold the entire batch for review: do not publish or execute any task until these are resolved and the batch is revalidated. Use [] when none remain. Questions explicitly assigned to a Research task belong in that task's scope instead.
